title: Multi-Variable Conformal Prediction: Optimizing Prediction Sets using Multiple Calibration Variables
claim: Prior methods split calibration data and tune one threshold, giving conservative, high-variance coverage; ours jointly optimizes and calibrates on all data for tighter coverage.
layout: Two parallel flowcharts around central data box, coverage distribution plot at bottom
description: Two vertical flowcharts sit side by side, with a shared grey 'Calibration data' box split into Subset 1 and Subset 2 in the middle. On the left, in orange, Standard Split Conformal Prediction runs top to bottom: Optimization of the prediction set, which takes Subset 1. Calibration of threshold q̃* ∈ ℝ, which takes Subset 2. Prediction set Ỹ(x, q̃*) = {y | s̃(x,y) ≤ q̃*}. On the right, in blue, Multi-Variable Conformal Prediction has a single Joint optimization and calibration box over parameters q* ∈ ℝ^nq, fed by the whole data box. It leads to the Prediction set Y(x, q*) = {y | s(x,y,q*) ≤ 0}. At the bottom, dotted arrows lead from each method to a coverage-probability plot. The orange curve is wide and sits to the right of a red dashed target-coverage line, labeled conservative, high variance. The blue curve is narrow and sits closer to the line, labeled tight, low variance. Color coding carries the contrast.
caption: To optimize the prediction-set shape, split conformal prediction (SCP) reserves part of the calibration data and calibrates a single threshold on the rest, whereas multi-variable conformal prediction (MCP) jointly optimizes and calibrates multiple shape parameters on all calibration data. Both can certify the high-confidence coverage guarantee P(η ≥1 −ε) ≥1 −β, but MCP yields a narrower and less conservative coverage distribution.
abstract: Split conformal prediction constructs prediction sets with finite-sample coverage guarantees, but its calibration stage is limited to adjusting a single threshold parameter. Hence, the shape of the prediction sets must be fixed beforehand, typically by fitting it on a reserved part of the calibration data. We introduce multi-variable conformal prediction (MCP), a framework that jointly optimizes and calibrates multiple prediction-set parameters in a single optimization problem, eliminating calibration data split without sacrificing finite-sample coverage guarantees. Building on scenario theory, a principled framework for certifying data-driven decisions, we propose two tractable variants: RemMCP, grounded in constrained optimization with constraint removal, which generalizes split conformal prediction; and RelMCP, based on penalized optimization with constraint relaxation, which also supports non-convex problems, albeit at a higher computational cost. In experiments with ellipsoidal and multi-modal prediction sets, RemMCP and a heuristic, adaptive version of RelMCP consistently meet the target coverage, with lower variance across calibration runs than baselines with calibration data split, and in most settings with smaller or comparable prediction sets.
